families.migration: Rebuild-only index; canonical identity is scoped tuple, never timestamp or project-only shorthand.
families.retention_compaction: Scoped idempotency identity persists for the app-data-root store lifetime and is not independently TTL-evicted.
families.redaction_no_secret_rule: Identity, semantic digest, append locator, and schema refs only.
families.legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status: Dedicated scoped idempotency accelerator; distinct from global event_id and lookup indexes.

families.replay_behavior: Current only when the cursor equals the verified seglog tail under the append-writer lock; behind, missing, or corrupt state forces synchronous catch-up or dedupe_unavailable without append.
families.migration: Rebuild with both dedicated dedupe indexes from authoritative seglog; never infer currentness from mtime.
families.retention_compaction: Source-coupled to the EventRecord identity indexes and replaced only by an atomically committed successor checkpoint.
families.redaction_no_secret_rule: Cursor, storage identity, digest, and timestamps only.
families.legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status: Separate currentness authority for both dedupe accelerators; not an EventRecord lookup row.

families.replay_behavior: Set and clear are durable authority transitions; legal holds never clear automatically and multiple holds compose by union.
families.migration: First distinct hold authority family; no prefix or mtime inference may synthesize or clear it.
families.retention_compaction: Authority receipts retain indefinitely and reach all named snapshot/blob/receipt dependencies.
families.redaction_no_secret_rule: Semantic scope and actor refs only; no raw local path or secret material.
families.legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status: Materialized owner row for legal, preserved, recent-run, and recovery hold authority.

families.replay_behavior: Blocked episode, safe point, snapshot refs, and anchor publish as one durability unit; only the three closed release reasons may release it.
families.migration: First distinct recovery-anchor family; absence never implies release.
families.retention_compaction: Open and recovery_unavailable anchors retain dependencies indefinitely; terminal authority remains queryable after release.
families.redaction_no_secret_rule: Semantic execution and snapshot refs only.
families.legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status: Distinct recovery anchor; not inferred from safe-point age or blocked projection convergence.

families.replay_behavior: Nonterminal operation plus same-directory manifest is reconciled before any new maintenance operation or writer startup.
families.migration: First canonical operation-history row; sidecar manifest remains the crash control authority for file promotion.
families.retention_compaction: Active operation is anchored; non-authority migration/recovery operational history retains 2,555 days unless a backup, rollback, hold, or audit ref is stronger.
families.redaction_no_secret_rule: Stable root/lease/manifest refs and hashes only.
families.legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status: One maintenance-lease history row shared by migration, compaction, restore, salvage, and backup-boundary capture.

families.replay_behavior: Exact raw bytes remain in same-filesystem quarantine custody; the row retains the custody manifest and append-ordered recovery receipts, and never normalizes or reinterprets the raw source.
families.migration: A registered upgrader acts only on a secured copy and CAS-publishes a validated successor; unknown schema remains recovery_blocked. Every resolution transition passes through secured.
families.retention_compaction: Value selects the exact Q risk policy; Q-CRITICAL is the family fail-safe default and unresolved critical items are never cap-evicted.
families.redaction_no_secret_rule: Routine exports exclude raw bytes; row contains hashes, redacted locators, bounded error metadata, and refs only.
families.legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status: Materialized quarantine authority replacing prose-only reset/quarantine behavior.

raw_custody_ref.description: Stable same-filesystem exact-byte custody ref; never a normalized replacement payload.

transition_receipts.description: Append-ordered state transitions. Readiness must prove first-from detected, continuity, current-state equality, and retained policy/hold evidence across the full array.

families.replay_behavior: Immediate logical hide and durable content-free deletion authority precede physical successor-generation purge; held/failed state remains visible and replayable.
families.migration: First canonical deletion-lifecycle family; project-list removal remains distinct and cannot create this row implicitly.
families.retention_compaction: Content-free tombstone and deletion/hold receipts remain indefinitely; deleted content purges from active canon within 24 hours unless held.
families.redaction_no_secret_rule: Tombstone never copies titles, message bodies, attachment bytes, prompts, tool output, or deleted content.
families.legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status: Canonical thread/project-data deletion lifecycle authority, separate from ordinary registry removal.

families.replay_behavior: Permission snapshots remain immutable attempt evidence and are not reconstructed from safe-point or restore-point state.
families.migration: Split from the mixed permission/safe-point/restore-point inventory without changing its canonical key.
families.retention_compaction: Follow attempt lineage and stronger preservation or hold rules owned by storage and Permissions_System.
families.redaction_no_secret_rule: Permission decisions and refs only; no credentials, tokens, or policy secrets.
families.deferred_reason: Nested permission value schema remains owner-routed and is outside the Case L registry-v2 materialization slice.
families.reopen_condition: Materialize when Permissions_System promotes the closed permission snapshot value schema.

families.replay_behavior: Resolve the exact immutable key and validated bytes; never reconstruct from current settings or a compatibility subset.
families.migration: No pre-existing shape is promoted as this family. A legacy ref is accepted only through the run-start v1-to-v2 upgrader in section 7.4 when it already resolves to this exact schema and identity.
families.retention_compaction: Retain at least as long as every referencing EventRecord and any applicable hold; after the last reference is released, normal policy eligibility may remove the exact record but never synthesize a replacement.
families.redaction_no_secret_rule: Store canonical IDs and non-secret owner refs only; reject raw credentials, tokens, auth values, credential paths, and local secrets.

families.replay_behavior: The tuple command_id, project_id, anchor_id, blocked_sequence, idempotency_key, and canonical_request_sha256 resolves to the original receipt and domain result. An exact replay performs no second transition, release, cleanup, or side effect; a conflicting request digest fails closed as invalid_args and never overwrites authority.
families.migration: First canonical recovery-unavailable resolution-receipt family. No command-local receipt, event payload, projection, anchor state, timestamp, UI acknowledgement, or legacy key is promoted or inferred as this authority.
families.retention_compaction: Retain receipt authority indefinitely. Compaction may rewrite only representation while preserving the exact receipt identity, canonical request digest, result, refs, replay result, and release authority; age, exit, archive, run completion, worktree unbinding, pressure, or cleanup never deletes it or releases an anchor.
families.redaction_no_secret_rule: Store stable non-secret identity, custody, confirmation, verification, and receipt refs plus hashes and closed enums only; never store raw paths, snapshot bytes, local-work bytes, credentials, tokens, secrets, provider output, or confirmation bodies.
families.legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status: Canonical recovery-unavailable command-resolution and anchor-release receipt; distinct from the EventRecord payload, recovery_anchor_record, UI acknowledgement, generic command result, and any command-local peer receipt.

value_schema.$comment: Behavioral equality not expressible by JSON Schema remains mandatory: before_snapshot_refs equals the admitted anchor set; abandonment and every nonsuccess preserve that set; locate success records exactly the owner-verified set; replay returns the original receipt byte-for-byte and performs no second state transition.

families.replay_behavior: Restore the last valid committed Home layout for the project/workspace tab. Preview frames are local and never written. Invalid, stale, corrupt, or off-screen records are rejected atomically and replaced by safe defaults with a visible recovery disposition.
families.migration: Read the canonical dotted key first, then the compatibility colon key through StorageMigrationCoordinator. Copy forward only after schema, identity, limit, and bounds validation; ambiguous project/workspace identity fails closed.
families.retention_compaction: Retain the latest valid committed layout plus one prior migration/recovery generation per project/workspace tab; never compact while a restore or migration receipt references the record.
families.redaction_no_secret_rule: Store stable surface/domain references, sizes, bounds, focus order, validation, and migration metadata only. Never persist buffers, file contents, terminal transcripts, PTYs, browser history, chat messages, credentials, or Dashboard widget layout.
families.legacy_canonical_crosswalk_status: New Home workspace family. Legacy dashboard_layout:v1, single-floating-editor, and two-section terminal layout are compatibility/source-lineage constraints and are not alternative Home authority.

value_schema.title: Puppet Master Home Workspace Layout V1
value_schema.description: Project/workspace-scoped presentation layout. It stores stable surface references only and never owns editor buffers, terminal sessions, PTYs, browser sessions, chat messages, or Dashboard widget layout.
